lines: Multi-agent wave (Analyst → Architect → QA → Dev ↔ Reviewer)

card.summary: Multi-agent feature wave. Analyst → Architect → QA → Dev with Reviewer gate between Dev and QA. Three approval gates, orchestrator-run interviews (subagents can't reach the user), tier-specialized Devs, suspicious-change tracking, reviewer_verdicts[] trail. --autonomous mode auto-approves all gates for unattended runs (never commits). Personas live in .claude/agents/.
card.paragraph: Drives a multi-agent feature wave. Spawns a worktree, interviews the user up front (orchestrator-run — agents that hit a blocking ambiguity hand back an open_questions[] block instead of asking directly), runs Analyst → Architect → QA in sequence (each behind a user gate unless --autonomous), then dispatches tier-specialized Dev agents under QA control until all tests are green.
use_when: Feature decomposes into multiple tasks across tiers
You want failing tests written before any code
You want a written architecture decision, not freeform
dontuse_when: Refactor with no behavior change (no failing test)

invocations.cmd: /stx-feature Implement multi-delete feature for Admins on Dashboard

invocations.comment: Autonomous — auto-approve all 3 gates; never commits
invocations.cmd: /stx-feature <o>--autonomous</o> Implement multi-delete feature for Admins on Dashboard

extras.title: Artifacts produced
rows: Canonical state — features, tasks, suspicious[], escalations[], gates[]

extras.title: Iteration caps
items: Soft cap 3 / task — Architect re-engages, may append Revision N to architecture-verse.
Hard cap 5 / task — wave halts, handoff.md written.
Suspicious-changes 3 / task — auto-halt task (scope-drift, test-file touch, mock-of-SUT, build-break).
Autonomous never bypasses reviewer halt verdicts, iteration caps, destructive ops, or commit/PR steps.
